children: Bamboo Insurance filed an S-1 to go public, with shares of its Class A common stock to be listed on the NYSE under the symbol “BMB.” This is an initial public offering in an Up-C structure, with selling stockholders offering the shares and the company receiving no proceeds. The filing highlights Bamboo’s AI-driven underwriting platform, diversified capacity relationships, and strong growth in the homeowners insurance market.

Bamboo Insurance is an AI- and technology-enabled managing general underwriter (MGU) focused on the homeowners insurance market. The company originates and services policies, handling data science, underwriting, policy administration, distribution, and claims on behalf of highly rated program partners, while bearing limited balance sheet risk. Its business model is capital-light, with revenue primarily from commissions paid by capacity providers and fees paid by policyholders. Bamboo operates two segments: (1) MGU, which includes the core underwriting platform and the Bamboo Agency retail channel; and (2) Bamboo Captive, a selective quota-share reinsurer used to align interests and support new market growth.

Bamboo differentiates itself through a modern, modular technology stack and proprietary decisioning engine (“Rhizome”) that integrates more than 200 data points per risk, enabling address-level aggregation controls, rapid product iteration, and high straight-through processing rates. The company partners with a diversified panel of 7 program partners, 60 global reinsurers, and 28 institutional investors participating through structures such as the $400 million Greenshoots Re sidecar and the $100 million Greengrove Re wildfire-focused CAT bond. Its distribution spans captive carrier agents, thousands of independent agencies, and embedded point‑of‑sale partnerships in real estate and mortgage ecosystems.
: The U.S. homeowners insurance market was ~$189 billion in annual premiums in 2025.
: The market grew at a ~10% CAGR since 2019; California at ~12% CAGR to ~$18 billion; Texas at ~12% CAGR to ~$20 billion.
: Bamboo reports ~4% California market share as of December 31, 2025 and loss ratios outperforming peers by an average of 32 percentage points over five years.
: Legacy admitted carriers, other MGUs/MGAs, and state residual market programs such as the California FAIR Plan.
: Rising catastrophe frequency/severity, growth of alternative reinsurance capital, increasing use of AI and analytics, and the rise of MGUs/MGAs.
: Policy retention was 88% for the twelve months ended June 30, 2026
: Operations centered in California and Texas, with plans to expand to additional states
: ~4% market share in California; entered Texas in September 2025
: 7 program partners, 60 reinsurers, and 28 institutional investors in sidecar/CAT bond capacity
: Managed Premium reached $766 million in 2025 and $879 million for the twelve months ended June 30, 2026

: ~85% straight-through processing; bindable quotes often in under five minutes; wrote ~$16 million in premium across ~6,000 policies in Texas through June 2026; ~3,500 independent agents in CA and ~2,000 in TX; won ~11% of new California homeowners policies in 2023
: Revenue of $173 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026
: MGU segment revenue up ~50% vs. the six months ended June 30, 2025
: Net income of $14 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026 (8% margin)
, Founder, Chief Executive Officer and Chairman - Former CEO of McGraw Group; operating roles at Altamont Capital and Golden Gate Capital; earlier at The Hartford; MBA from NYU Stern.
, Chief Financial Officer - Former SVP & CFO of the Property & Casualty Division at Kemper; leadership roles at Travelers; BS in Mathematics from Lafayette College.
, Chief Insurance Officer - Former Chief Actuary at Safe‑Guard Products; prior Chief Actuary and SVP Product Management at CSAA Insurance Group; BA and MBA from UC Berkeley.
, Chief Operating Officer - Previously Bamboo’s Chief Revenue Officer and CFO; former executive at Kemper and EY; CPA (inactive); BSBA from Miami University.
: J.P. Morgan; Morgan Stanley; Deutsche Bank Securities; Evercore ISI; Wells Fargo Securities
: The company will not receive any proceeds; the selling stockholders are offering the shares. The purpose is to create a public market and facilitate future capital access.
